# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** CountyCare — Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:**
Riley Grant
Member ID: W485404613
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-09 — Reference number POC-5767D9118E-71989**
**Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Governing policy:** *EVH CG 2734.CC Outpatient Major Joint Arthroplasty (Hips and Knees)* — https://countycare.com/wp-content/uploads/ECG_2734.CC-for-Outpatient-Major-Joint-Arthroplasy-Hips-and-Knees-ver-Dec-25.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing CountyCare's denial of the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) requested by my surgeon. The notice dated 2026-08-09 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because my medical records contain the imaging findings the plan's own published guideline identifies, and my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this surgery is needed.

Below I set my records against the language of the plan's own guideline, quoted word for word.

## 1. The imaging findings in my chart are the findings the plan's guideline lists

The guideline lists, among its clinical findings:

> "● Effusions ● Acute fracture ● Avascular necrosis ● Joint space narrowing or large osteophytes on imaging ● Severe sclerosis or deformity ● Bone on bone contact WITH At least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (6,16,17):"

My records establish these findings:

- **Imaging dated 2026-05-30 — MRI of the knee:** full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment **with bone-on-bone apposition**; Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially.

That is the "Bone on bone contact" item in the plan's own list, documented on imaging, at the most advanced radiographic grade. I respectfully ask the reviewer to look again at the MRI report of 2026-05-30 before any further determination is made, because the stated reason for the denial rests on imaging, and the imaging in my file reports exactly what the guideline describes.

## 2. My non-surgical treatment is documented

The same guideline language requires "At least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record." My records show:

- **NSAIDs for 8 months** with inadequate relief.
- **Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-19**, which gave 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Supervised physical therapy**, quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, **2026-05-15 to 2026-07-10 — 8 weeks, 18 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

Taken together, my documented course of non-surgical treatment spans well beyond 12 weeks and includes medication, injection, and supervised therapy. It did not resolve my symptoms.

## 3. My documented symptoms and function

- 9 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3 to 4 times nightly with pain.
- Exam: positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain.
- No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

## 4. Two points about how the guideline was applied

First, the criteria quoted above appear in the guideline under the heading:

> "Replacement/revision of previous arthroplasty Replacement/revision TKA or THA may be considered necessary as an inpatient procedure when the following criteria are met:"

The surgery my surgeon requested is a partial knee replacement, CPT 27446. If the plan applied replacement/revision criteria, or the section beginning "LIMITATIONS FOR OUTPATIENT TKA OR THA The following criteria deems outpatient TKA or THA as not appropriate:", I ask that this be stated plainly in the appeal decision, along with an explanation of why those criteria govern my request.

Second, the guideline states:

> "● Where a specific clinical indication is not directly addressed in this guideline, medical necessity determination will be made based on widely accepted standard of care criteria."

The guideline also states that:

> "These criteria are supported by evidence-based or peer-reviewed sources such as medical literature, societal guidelines, and state/national recommendations."

and that:

> "● The guideline criteria in the following sections were developed utilizing evidence-based and peer-reviewed resources from medical publications and societal organization guidelines as well as from widely accepted standard of care, best practice recommendations."

By the plan's own terms, then, if my indication is not directly addressed by a listed section, the decision is to be made on widely accepted standard of care. My chart documents end-stage medial compartment disease on MRI, months of failed medication, a failed injection, completed supervised physical therapy, night pain, and loss of function — and a treating orthopedic surgeon who has documented that the procedure is needed.

I want to be clear about one thing for the reviewer's benefit: apart from the passages quoted above, I am not quoting the plan's criteria, because the full criteria applied to my case have not been provided to me. Everything else in this letter is my own description of my records.

## Request for the criteria that were actually applied

**I am requesting, in writing and free of charge, the specific rule, guideline, or criterion relied upon to deny my request.** I understand my plan uses InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a public document. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to provide the specific rule or criterion relied on for an adverse determination at no cost to me. I am therefore asking CountyCare to send me **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, together with the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made this decision. Without that, I cannot fully address the basis of the denial, and I ask that the plan supply it before the appeal is decided.

## What I am asking for

I ask CountyCare to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-09 and authorize the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) requested by Dr. Marchetti. I ask that a physician reviewer in orthopedic surgery review the MRI report of 2026-05-30, the physical therapy discharge note, and my surgeon's operative request.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, **by 2027-02-05**, and I am submitting it within that time. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if there is a different or additional address for member appeals, please tell me and I will resend it there. (Other members reading this: call the number on the back of your insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.)

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-09 (Reference POC-5767D9118E-71989)
- MRI report dated 2026-05-30
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-15 to 2026-07-10, 18 visits)
- Medication and injection records, including corticosteroid injection 2026-05-19
- Office notes and surgical request from Dr. Marchetti, orthopedic surgery
- [Any other records I am including]

Thank you for taking a careful second look at my file. I can be reached at [my phone number] or [my email address] if anything further is needed.

Sincerely,

**Riley Grant**
Member ID: W485404613
Reference number: POC-5767D9118E-71989
[Signature]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
